question: In the standard metric BMI formula, how is height measured?

options.A: Inches
options.B: Centimeters
options.C: Meters squared
options.D: Millimeters

explanation: The standard metric formula needs height in meters, which you then square. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h2)

question: Why is the left anterior descending (LAD) artery famously called the widow-maker?

options.A: It carries deoxygenated blood back to the lungs.
options.B: It is the longest vein in the human heart.
options.C: It supplies blood to the major pumping walls of the left ventricle.
options.D: It controls the electrical rhythm of the heart valves.

explanation: Spot on! The LAD feeds the thick, heavy-duty walls of the left ventricle. If it gets blocked, the heart's main pumping power is severely crippled. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h1)

question: What does your skin do when you step into a cold environment?

options.A: Blood vessels in the skin widen to let heat out
options.B: Sweat glands release extra cooling fluid
options.C: Melanocytes produce more dark pigment
options.D: Blood vessels in the skin narrow to hold in body heat

explanation: Well done! When it's cold, your blood vessels squeeze shut near the surface to keep your warm blood safely around your inner organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is giving pain meds around the clock better than waiting for 'PRN' (as needed) requests in chronic pain?

options.A: It completely eliminates the possibility of experiencing side effects
options.B: It ensures family members can control the medication schedule easily
options.C: It maintains steady blood levels and prevents severe pain spikes
options.D: It reduces the total drug dosage required to zero within a week

explanation: Scheduled dosing keeps a steady guard up in the blood, stopping pain from roaring back before the next dose. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h7)

question: What type of strong connective tissue attaches skeletal muscles directly to bones?

options.A: Tendon
options.B: Synovium
options.C: Ligament
options.D: Cartilage

explanation: You got it! Tendons connect muscle to bone (remember: 'T'endon = 'T'ies muscle to bone), while ligaments connect bone to bone. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why should a nurse study local disease patterns before planning a health talk?

options.A: To fulfill a mandatory administrative file requirement for the federal ministry
options.B: To guarantee that every single household receives identical instructions
options.C: To ensure the teaching targets the actual health challenges facing that specific community
options.D: To prove that modern medicine is superior to traditional healing methods

explanation: Well done! Every community is unique. Knowing their specific challenges helps you focus on what actually matters to them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h2)

question: In simple terms, what does endocrine 'hyposecretion' mean?

options.A: Hormones are destroyed in the bloodstream
options.B: A gland produces too little of a hormone
options.C: A gland produces too much of a hormone
options.D: Target organs completely reject hormones

explanation: You've got this! 'Hypo-' always means under or low. So hyposecretion just means the gland isn't making enough hormone. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h1)

question: What is the main reason a community clinic keeps a dedicated referral register book?

options.A: To advertise traditional medicine options to local residents
options.B: To calculate the monthly salaries of visiting medical doctors
options.C: To record the personal daily attendance of nursing staff members
options.D: To track outgoing cases, dates, and receiving facilities for auditing

explanation: Brilliant! Logging every referral helps clinics keep a clean record of who was sent out, when, and where they went. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h8)

question: Why do some rectally administered drugs avoid the liver's first-pass metabolism?

options.A: The rectal wall completely destroys all liver enzymes
options.B: Lymph nodes absorb the entire dose before it reaches blood vessels
options.C: Lower rectal veins drain directly into systemic circulation
options.D: Medications bypass the bloodstream and enter the kidneys

explanation: Blood from the inferior rectal veins goes straight to the inferior vena cava, bypassing the liver on its first trip around the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h2)

question: A patient is asked to stand up from a chair, walk ten feet, turn around, and sit back down. What is this clinical observation called?

options.A: Pulmonary function trial
options.B: Cardiorespiratory stress exam
options.C: Get-Up-and-Go test
options.D: Neurological reflex screen

explanation: The Get-Up-and-Go test is a quick, practical way to evaluate a patient's balance, sit-to-stand transition, and walking stability. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h3)

question: Patient, health, environment, and nursing. Why are these four big ideas so special in our field?

options.A: They represent the four core pillars that define nursing practice
options.B: They are required elements for hospital budget planning
options.C: They determine the legal penalties for medical malpractice
options.D: They outline the exact daily schedule for ward nurses

explanation: Spot on! These four concepts make up the 'metaparadigm' of nursing—basically, the big four pillars that every single nursing theory builds upon. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: What important instruction should a nurse give a patient who has received dilating eye drops?

options.A: Wear heavy winter gloves to avoid rubbing the eyelids
options.B: Avoid driving because their vision will be temporarily blurred
options.C: Keep their eyes tightly closed for the rest of the day
options.D: Wash their eyes thoroughly with tap water every ten minutes

explanation: Dilating drops paralyze the focusing muscles and dilate the pupil, causing blurry vision and glare, making driving unsafe. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h5)

question: What type of germ causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: A bacterium
options.B: A protozoan
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A prion

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny, single-celled parasite (a protozoan) that loves to cause irritation and unusual discharge. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h2)

question: A 16-year-old girl drops out of school due to an unplanned pregnancy. What long-term impact is she most likely to face?

options.A: Immediate government employment
options.B: Automatic university admission
options.C: Lifelong economic hardship
options.D: Complete immunity from malaria

explanation: Interrupting education early often limits future career opportunities, leading to long-term financial struggles. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: How do you check a baby's head sutures and fontanelles during a vaginal examination?

options.A: Shining a specialized light beam through the maternal abdomen
options.B: Measuring the external abdominal girth with a tape measure
options.C: Listening for echoes with a wooden stethoscope
options.D: Palpating the presenting part with a sterile gloved finger

explanation: You gently feel (palpate) the baby's head using a sterile gloved finger during an internal check to identify the fontanelles and sutures. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier keeping men away from health clinics?

options.A: Staff attitudes that treat men as unwelcome intruders
options.B: Clinics operating convenient evening and weekend hours
options.C: Long waiting times that clash with work schedules
options.D: Facility environments focused solely on mothers and babies

explanation: Convenient operating hours would actually encourage attendance, whereas the other options represent real barriers men face. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: Why is it so important to chew your food thoroughly before swallowing?

options.A: To activate salivary lipase completely inside the mouth
options.B: To increase the surface area of food for better enzyme action
options.C: To remove all bacteria before the food enters the esophagus
options.D: To change the chemical pH of the food from acidic to basic

explanation: Chewing breaks big chunks of food into tiny pieces. This gives digestive enzymes a much larger surface area to work on, making digestion way more efficient! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h2)

question: How does chronic psychological stress typically affect food cravings?

options.A: It increases a natural desire for raw vegetables and water
options.B: It raises cortisol and triggers cravings for fatty, sugary foods
options.C: It forces the digestive system to absorb fewer total calories
options.D: It completely stops the body from digesting any proteins

explanation: You got it! High cortisol from stress tricks the brain into seeking out dense, comforting, high-calorie foods for quick energy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication that can significantly influence a patient interaction?

options.A: The specific medical terminology used in the care plan
options.B: Open posture and relaxed facial expressions
options.C: A printed schedule of clinic operating hours
options.D: The speed at which discharge instructions are read aloud

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions are non-verbal cues that convey openness, empathy, or disinterest without using words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h2)

question: What is a key requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method to remain effective as contraception?

options.A: Taking daily iron supplements along with herbal teas
options.B: Switching to infant formula feeds after the first month
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding without supplementary feeds and no return of menses
options.D: Using male condoms during every third act of sexual intercourse

explanation: LAM relies on frequent suckling hormones to suppress ovulation, but it only works if breastfeeding is exclusive and menstruation has not resumed. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: A nurse sits at the patient's eye level, listens softly, and repeats back key points the patient shared. What is the nurse showing?

options.A: Passive observation and clinical delegation
options.B: Routine administrative record keeping
options.C: Aggressive interrogation and data gathering
options.D: Active listening and therapeutic communication

explanation: These simple bedside actions make a patient feel truly heard, respected, and safe with you. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h4)

question: Why is obstructed labor more common among very young mothers?

options.A: Cephalopelvic disproportion caused by an immature pelvis
options.B: Premature hardening of the fetal cranial bones
options.C: Excessive physical exercise during the third trimester
options.D: Over-consumption of dietary iron during the first trimester

explanation: Spot on! Because a young girl's pelvis is still growing, it might be too small for the baby's head to pass through easily. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h4)

question: A ward wants to start using digital health tools. What step best helps make this happen?

options.A: Destroying all computers to force staff to use paper notebooks
options.B: Training staff on electronic health record systems and telehealth tools
options.C: Stopping all clinical research activities in the facility
options.D: Banning patients from using mobile phones inside hospital rooms

explanation: Well done! Going digital successfully always starts with properly training the nurses on how to use the new tech. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h7)

question: How do a patient's cultural beliefs usually affect their healthcare journey?

options.A: They have no impact once formal hospital medications are ordered
options.B: They only influence dietary choices and never affect medication use
options.C: They dictate the exact insurance plan the client is allowed to hold
options.D: They shape how the client interprets illness and chooses treatments

explanation: Spot on! Culture is like a lens. It determines whether someone sees a symptom as spiritual, natural, or medical, and who they go to for help first. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a necessary step when receiving new stock on the ward?

options.A: Verifying that the expiration dates on the products are acceptable
options.B: Checking the physical items against the quantities on the delivery note
options.C: Hiding the delivery notes so other staff members cannot read them
options.D: Inspecting the packaging for any signs of damage or leakage

explanation: Delivery notes are official records that should be kept accessible for audits, not hidden away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why isn't the CA-125 blood test used as a general screening tool for healthy women?

options.A: It only detects cancer after it has already spread to the brain
options.B: It requires a painful surgical biopsy before the blood sample is drawn
options.C: It can be elevated by non-cancerous conditions like endometriosis or menstruation
options.D: The cost of the test is too high for public healthcare systems

explanation: You nailed it. Normal things like your period or harmless cysts can also make CA-125 levels rise, leading to false alarms. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h5)

question: Which of these habits helps keep oral syringes clean and free of germs?

options.A: Rinsing the dirty syringe in a shared sink basin
options.B: Storing open syringes in a warm pocket all day
options.C: Avoiding touching the syringe tip to any surface
options.D: Touching the tip directly to the patient's tongue

explanation: Keep that tip sterile! Touching it to counters or fingers can introduce unwanted bacteria right back into the medicine bottle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h5)

question: Why is teamwork across different sectors necessary when addressing the health needs of unemployed persons?

options.A: Joblessness affects multiple aspects of life that healthcare alone cannot fix
options.B: Medical clinics have unlimited funds for business startups
options.C: Nurses are legally forbidden from talking to social workers
options.D: Government agencies prefer to work in complete isolation

explanation: Correct! Unemployment involves housing, food, and financial needs that require teamwork across different community sectors. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h7)

question: How does long-term intestinal schistosomiasis end up causing portal hypertension?

options.A: Adult worms multiply rapidly inside the heart and increase overall blood pressure.
options.B: Intestinal bleeding drains blood volume, forcing the heart to pump at a dangerous rate.
options.C: The kidneys fail to filter salt, causing fluid overload throughout the entire body.
options.D: Trapped eggs cause liver fibrosis that blocks blood flow through the portal vein system.

explanation: When eggs get trapped in the liver, the body forms scar tissue (fibrosis). This traffic jam blocks normal blood flow, raising pressure in the portal vein. Pathophysiology made clear! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h7)

question: Which dressing type is made from seaweed and is best suited for wounds with heavy drainage?

options.A: Dry gauze sponge
options.B: Transparent film
options.C: Alginate
options.D: Hydrocolloid

explanation: Alginate dressings absorb large amounts of wound exudate by forming a soft gel, making them ideal for bleeding or heavily draining wounds. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a draw sheet placed across the middle of a hospital bed?

options.A: To replace the need for a standard bottom sheet
options.B: To help lift, turn, and reposition the patient easily
options.C: To serve as an extra blanket during cold night shifts
options.D: To catch food crumbs during meal delivery times

explanation: Correct! A draw sheet acts like a handy helper, letting you slide or turn a patient smoothly without causing friction burns or shear injuries. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h3)

question: What do we call a loss that can be clearly seen and verified by everyone around, like losing a limb or a loved one?

options.A: A loss that is only felt internally by the affected individual
options.B: A loss of money or property caused by economic changes
options.C: A loss that occurs only during old age and natural retirement
options.D: A loss that can be recognized and verified by other people

explanation: Spot on! An actual loss is tangible. It's something both the patient and outsiders can clearly see, touch, or acknowledge, like an amputation or death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h1)

question: When should hand hygiene be performed during a physical examination?

options.A: At the end of the entire shift
options.B: Only when the patient has a known infection
options.C: Before and after touching the patient
options.D: Only if the nurse's hands look visibly dirty

explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most effective way to stop the spread of germs between patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: What does having 'psychological safety' mean for a nursing team?

options.A: Patients receive regular psychological counseling during hospital admission
options.B: Team members feel safe to speak up, question orders, and share concerns without fear
options.C: Wards are kept completely quiet at night to reduce stress
options.D: Doctors maintain absolute authority without input from nursing staff

explanation: Exactly! Psychological safety means even a junior nurse can point out a dangerous order without worrying about being insulted or victimized. [learn more](GST319_U5_T3#GST319_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why might two patients who had the exact same surgery report completely different pain levels?

options.A: One patient is always just exaggerating their discomfort
options.B: Hospital room temperatures change how nerves send distress signals
options.C: Surgical skill varies so much that tissue injury is never identical
options.D: Pain involves emotional and cultural factors, not just physical injury

explanation: Spot on! Pain isn't just about the physical cut. A person's emotions, background, and past experiences all change how they feel and express pain. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h1)

question: When would you choose an intramuscular injection instead of giving pills by mouth?

options.A: When the patient cannot take oral medications
options.B: When the patient wants to avoid any skin punctures
options.C: When the medication needs to work over a full week
options.D: When the drug is completely harmless to the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is vomiting or unable to swallow, going through the muscle is a safe and reliable backup plan. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must vaccine and medication storage refrigerators have their temperatures checked and recorded regularly?

options.A: To ensure the refrigerator door is locked at all times
options.B: To check if the electricity bill is too high for the ward
options.C: To make sure improper heat does not ruin drug potency
options.D: To calculate how many patients received injections that day

explanation: Many pharmaceutical products degrade quickly if temperatures fluctuate outside the safe cold chain range. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: What is the main reason doctors taper corticosteroid therapy down gradually instead of stopping it overnight?

options.A: To prevent the development of severe allergic skin rashes
options.B: To keep blood sugar levels artificially low during withdrawal
options.C: To allow the adrenal glands time to resume natural cortisol production
options.D: To ensure the original disease symptoms never return again

explanation: A slow taper gives the sleeping adrenal glands a gentle wakeup call so they can remember how to make their own cortisol again safely. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h8)

question: What should you do if a patient pushes out a suppository right after you insert it?

options.A: Inspect the stool, check the status, and consult the prescriber for a repeat dose
options.B: Immediately force a second suppository into the rectum without checking
options.C: Assume the full dose was already absorbed and document successful administration
options.D: Scold the patient for failing to hold the medication inside the bowel

explanation: If it comes out whole before melting, the dose is lost, and you must check with the prescriber before trying again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h8)

question: A patient with severe pre-eclampsia is being transferred from a primary health center to a teaching hospital. What must the midwife send along?

options.A: The patient's birth certificate and national identity card
options.B: A formal resignation letter on behalf of the medical officer
options.C: The keys to the primary health center's main pharmaceutical store
options.D: Clear, written documentation of all assessments and treatments given

explanation: Accompanying documentation ensures the receiving team knows what interventions have already been done, preventing delays. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h6)

question: What is a very common underlying cause of autonomic neuropathy in clinical practice?

options.A: Severe bone fractures
options.B: Acute muscle strain
options.C: Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic iron deficiency

explanation: Over time, persistently high blood sugar levels damage peripheral nerves. This makes diabetic autonomic neuropathy a frequent finding you will encounter in clinical wards. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which bone forms the large, flared upper part of the hip bone?

options.A: Ilium
options.B: Coccyx
options.C: Pubis
options.D: Ischium

explanation: The ilium is the broad, upper fan-shaped section of the hip bone that you feel on your waist. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h1)

question: A patient is unconscious and has a living will that lists specific rejected treatments, but a brand-new medical complication arises that is not mentioned in the paper. What is the main limitation of relying solely on the living will here?

options.A: Living wills automatically expire after five years in the hospital
options.B: Living wills can be too rigid to cover every unexpected clinical situation
options.C: Living wills only apply to surgical procedures, not medical treatments
options.D: Living wills must be approved by a judge before nurses can read them

explanation: Because a living will is a written list, it cannot anticipate every medical scenario, which is why having a healthcare proxy is also valuable. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which leadership style is most appropriate during a sudden emergency like a code blue?

options.A: Autocratic
options.B: Participative
options.C: Democratic
options.D: Laissez-faire

explanation: Autocratic leadership relies on fast, centralized commands, which are essential when every second counts during a crisis. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h3)

question: A community health nurse sees poor nutrition in a crowded neighborhood with many empty lots. What is a practical step to take?

options.A: Setting up community gardens and urban farming projects on the vacant lots
options.B: Building a large international shipping port in the city center
options.C: Replacing all local food markets with fast-food outlets
options.D: Encouraging residents to travel out of state for grocery shopping

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Turning empty lots into gardens is a brilliant way to fight nutritional deserts and bring fresh food to the community. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h3)

question: What are the main signs that a family caregiver is suffering from severe burnout?

options.A: A sudden desire to pursue advanced nursing degrees
options.B: Exhaustion, resentment, and emotional exhaustion
options.C: Improved physical strength and restful sleep patterns
options.D: Increased energy and excitement for daily tasks

explanation: Caring for others 24/7 is draining. When a caregiver is completely burnt out, they feel emotionally fried, bone-tired, and sometimes overwhelmed with resentment. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which physical sign tells you right away that a patient is getting dehydrated?

options.A: Flushed and warm skin
options.B: Moist, pink mucous membranes
options.C: Dry, cracked mucous membranes
options.D: Bounding peripheral pulses

explanation: Dry mouth and lips are classic, quick red flags that the body is low on water. Always check the mucous membranes during your assessments! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h3)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and drugs here in Nigeria?

options.A: WHO
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: FMOH
options.D: NMNC

explanation: Correct! NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) keeps our drug supply safe across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h6)

question: After a diagnostic laparoscopy, a patient complains of sharp shoulder pain. What is likely going on?

options.A: Severe emotional anxiety manifesting as physical upper body tension
options.B: A torn shoulder muscle from positioning on the operating table
options.C: Residual carbon dioxide gas irritating the diaphragm
options.D: An allergic reaction to the skin antiseptic applied before surgery

explanation: Correct! The gas used to puff up the tummy during surgery can drift up and irritate the diaphragm, causing a weird referred pain in the shoulder. It passes soon! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h7)

question: A patient arrives at the ward with a large amount of cash and expensive jewelry. What should the nurse do first regarding these valuables?

options.A: Tell the patient to wear the jewelry so nobody can steal it
options.B: Lock the cash inside the bedside table drawer and keep the key
options.C: Place the items in the open utility room for safe keeping
options.D: Follow hospital policy to document and secure the items safely

explanation: Valuables must be documented on an inventory list and stored securely according to hospital protocol, preferably sent home with family or locked in the main safe. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: How do vaccines protect the human body against specific diseases?

options.A: Destroying all bacteria currently living in the gut
options.B: Increasing the overall body temperature to kill viruses
options.C: Stimulating antibody production without causing illness
options.D: Providing permanent chemical antibiotics in the blood

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines introduce harmless pieces or weakened parts of a germ so your immune system can safely learn to fight it without getting you sick. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h1)

question: What molecule is the immediate source of chemical energy used for muscle contraction?

options.A: Creatine phosphate
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Glycogen
options.D: ATP

explanation: ATP supplies the necessary energy for myosin heads to move and detach during the contraction cycle. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h6)

question: If an evaluation is reliable, what does that tell us about its results?

options.A: Zero cost for the institution
options.B: That the test measures the exact right topic
options.C: Consistent and reproducible results over time
options.D: Instant passing grades for everyone

explanation: Think of reliability like a good weighing scale: if you step on it ten times in a row, it should give you the exact same weight every time. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a safe injection in clinical practice?

options.A: It cures the patient's illness within twenty-four hours.
options.B: It costs less than oral medications of the same class.
options.C: It is always administered intravenously using a metal needle.
options.D: It causes no harm to the patient and poses no risk to the provider.

explanation: A safe injection is defined primarily by its lack of harm to the recipient and the healthcare worker giving it. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h1)

question: A hospital board decides to build three new community health centers over the next four years. What type of objective does this represent?

options.A: Strategic objective
options.B: Individual performance objective
options.C: Daily shift objective
options.D: Operational objective

explanation: Long-term, multi-year plans involving major resource commitments are classic examples of strategic objectives. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which group of people often acts as a bridge between local communities and clinical PAC facilities?

options.A: Hospital maintenance staff
options.B: International tax auditors
options.C: Community health workers
options.D: Forensic investigators

explanation: Correct! Community health workers play a wonderful role in guiding patients to local support networks and follow-up care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h6)

question: Why do patients with severe anxiety often complain of dry mouth and stomach upset?

options.A: Patients with anxiety forget to drink water for many days.
options.B: Anxiety causes the stomach to produce too much digestive acid.
options.C: Stress hormones divert blood flow away from the digestive tract.
options.D: The liver stops processing bile during stressful moments.

explanation: Your body prioritizes surviving an immediate threat by sending blood to your muscles instead of your stomach, which puts digestion on pause. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h5)

question: Which of these practices helps stop clinical errors during tricky or high-risk procedures?

options.A: Discouraging nurses from reporting small near misses
options.B: Using standardized checklists and safety protocols
options.C: Allowing staff to work longer shifts without taking breaks
options.D: Removing all electronic monitoring devices from the ward

explanation: You nailed it! Checklists make sure we never skip critical steps, keeping both patients and busy nurses safe. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h7)

question: Through which pathway do surgeons typically reach the pituitary gland during a transsphenoidal hypophysectomy?

options.A: Through a large incision made just above the right ear
options.B: Through a small opening cut directly in the upper jawbone
options.C: Through the nasal cavity and the sphenoid sinus
options.D: Through the back of the neck right near the brainstem

question: What is the main reason doctors perform a liver biopsy?

question: What is often the most reliable early warning sign of an infection in a patient with a very weak immune system?

question: What is the main job of oxytocin during breastfeeding?

question: At what angle should an intramuscular injection be inserted into the skin?

question: What makes the copper IUD special compared to emergency contraceptive pills?

question: What does professional 'accountability' mean for a nurse on duty?

question: You notice an unresponsive patient has noisy, gurgling breathing. What should be your very first nursing action?

question: Why does breastfeeding usually demand more energy and nutrition from a mother than pregnancy did?

question: What is the bioavailability of a medication given directly through an intravenous (IV) line?

question: What practical change can nurses advocate for to help more men attend clinics?

question: Why must you check the expiration date on test strips before using them?

question: A patient is bleeding steadily with dark red blood from a laceration. Which vessel is most likely involved?

question: What is the big plus of choosing a no-scalpel vasectomy over the older method?

question: Why must health education topics change as children grow older?

question: A patient with mild kidney disease is denied a standard heart medication because the doctor worries about organ damage. What does this show?

question: What is a cystocele?

question: What happens to a Plaster of Paris cast if it gets wet?

question: A patient's waste moves through the colon at a normal speed, but they still struggle with hard stools and straining because of their diet. What do we call this type of constipation?

question: If an older adult is denied necessary food, medication, and basic hygiene, what type of abuse is this?

question: What is the main feature of a community-based organization (CBO)?

question: How does Maslow's hierarchy of needs apply to nursing school and patient care?

question: When one mature cell type changes into another mature cell type due to ongoing irritation, what is it called?

question: What information does the vestibular cortex primarily process?

question: A baby is born limp, pale, and quiet after a home delivery. What should you do right away?

question: What is the main goal of advance care planning discussions?

question: Which bleeding pattern is a serious warning sign (red flag) after a medical abortion?

question: What is the most serious, life-threatening side effect nurses must watch out for when giving opioids?

question: What is the main job of a nursing unit manager?

question: Which layer of a blood vessel wall is primarily responsible for regulating vessel diameter and blood pressure?

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal function or feature of the large intestine?

question: What is the most common cause of injuries to the brain and spine in our communities?

options.A: Workplace chemical exposure
options.B: Congenital weakness

explanation: You got it! High-speed car and motorcycle crashes unfortunately top the list as the leading cause of traumatic brain and spinal injuries globally. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is saliva's main job when you take a bite of food?

options.A: Absorbing simple sugars directly into the bloodstream

question: What did ancient Egyptians mix into vaginal pastes to block sperm?

question: Which hormone do the kidneys produce to tell the bone marrow to make red blood cells?

question: What is the main way beta-blockers help the heart?

options.A: Blocking the reabsorption of sodium in the renal tubules
options.B: Decreasing heart rate and force of myocardial contraction
options.C: Triggering rapid constriction of peripheral blood vessels
options.D: Stimulating the release of renin directly from the kidneys

explanation: Exactly! Beta-blockers tell the heart to slow down and beat a bit softer, giving overworked heart muscle a much-needed rest. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is considered a safe and realistic weekly weight loss target for most adults?

question: What happens to a joint capsule when severe inflammation occurs?

question: What is usually the main cause behind an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

question: A patient returns three days after an abortion with fever, lower tummy pain, and a bad-smelling discharge. What does this point to?

question: What is the medical term for the body's steady internal balance?

options.A: Metabolism

options.C: Catabolism

question: What does a drug's 'half-life' actually measure?

options.A: The time it takes for blood concentration to decrease by half

question: What is the main job of a medical bougie?

options.A: To deliver high-flow oxygen therapy
options.B: To monitor internal body temperature
options.C: To navigate or explore narrow passages
options.D: To permanently remove tissue masses

question: Who should a patient avoid getting too close to for a few hours right after a PET scan?

question: What is the primary advantage of mobile health clinics in reproductive health outreach?

options.B: Replacing all permanent hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Eliminating the need for community health education
options.D: Bringing family planning supplies directly to remote villages

question: What is the most frequent cause of acquired hypoparathyroidism?

options.C: Accidental surgical removal during neck surgery

question: A patient is given a medication with strong anticholinergic properties. As a nurse, what side effect should you watch out for?

options.C: Dry mouth and trouble urinating

question: What usually happens if food travels through the small intestine much faster than normal?

question: When starting a heart failure patient on a new beta-blocker, what is the safest way to begin?

question: After giving a patient a strong painkiller through an IV, what is your most important follow-up duty?

options.C: Document that the patient is cured of all chronic illnesses

question: Where is laboratory research typically carried out?

question: A patient gets a known surgical complication even though you followed all safety rules. Is this malpractice?

question: Which layer of the skin acts as the anchor, attaching the skin to muscles and bones underneath?

question: What is the most effective way for nurses to help eliminate the practice of gishiri cutting in rural communities?

question: Which lab test does a nurse watch closely when checking for a worsening skin infection?

question: What is the main difference between a sedative and a hypnotic drug?

question: What is endometritis?

question: What is the main energy source for a healthy, resting heart?

question: What is the main goal of using clot-busting (thrombolytic) therapy in an acute ischemic stroke?

question: What usually causes Transfusion-Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO)?

question: What happens in a Type I error during research?

question: You want to use EBP to manage a patient's wound. What should you consider alongside research articles?

question: Which sign shows that the body can no longer compensate for blood loss?

question: What is the main job of the fluid found inside the protective sac around the heart (pericardium)?

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized factor that influences a patient's ability to adapt to an illness?

question: How do you put together a complete nutritional care plan as a nurse?

question: Why is keeping furniture in the same place important for someone with low vision?

question: When would a clinician choose indirect ophthalmoscopy over direct ophthalmoscopy?

question: What does cultural competence require a nurse to do?

question: Where does a non-competitive antagonist usually bind on a cell receptor?

question: Why is regular skin monitoring necessary while a poultice is in place?

question: Why do healthcare programs designed only by adults often fail young people?

question: A healthy child receives a routine measles vaccine at the local health clinic. What type of immunity is being stimulated?

question: A patient's adult children demand you stop pain meds because of fear of addiction, but the alert patient wants relief. Whose wish wins?

question: What makes adaptive immunity different from innate immunity?

question: Why must medical waste be burned in an incinerator or buried deep instead of going to a normal dump?

question: Which global region currently has the highest number of maternal deaths?

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four key elements needed to prove malpractice?

question: What is Vitamin K's main role when it comes to blood clotting?

question: Why do fertility specialists always insist on evaluating both partners during a fertility workup?

question: A bedridden patient on fluid restriction needs a daily weight check. What is the most important step to make sure the reading is correct?
